title: Tenant-aware prewarm and soft-failure protocols for hosted GPU pools
creator: Lin Chen
description:
Summary:
During a hosted API capacity incident on 2026-03-06 we observed rapid queue amplification across multiple GPU pools driven by a combination of KV-cache pollution and autoscaler hysteresis. The observed failure mode: small burst of high-cardinality short-lived requests caused low cache hit-rate, which increased per-request GPU work. Autoscaler smoothing delayed capacity priming and the request queue increased exponentially, triggering tenant-impacting throttles.

Root causes (evidence):
- KV-cache pollution: high variance in prompt prefixes and a few tenants with noisy prefixes caused eviction of hot tenant entries (dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinfra/internal/d/kv-cache/kv-pollution-2026-03-06).
- Autoscaler hysteresis: the autoscaler uses a 60s smoothing window and requires sustained load to scale; short fast ramps were not captured. Logs: https://logs.redwoodinfra/internal/hosted/incident-2026-03-06.
- Lack of tenant-aware admission: all traffic shared a single admission surface; noisy tenants could amplify queue for others.

Impact:
- ~15% of production requests experienced >2s additional tail latency for 18 minutes; several customers reported degradation (support ticket cluster: INC-2026-4112).

Proposed mitigations (high level):
1) Tenant-aware prewarm signal: introduce a lightweight forecast signal that considers per-tenant recent rate-of-change to trigger prewarm workers earlier than the steady-state scaler.
2) Soft-failure/graded-degrade path: automatic fallback to a compatible, smaller/quantized model variant (same response schema) when the queue exceeds a threshold for a tenant. This keeps availability while reducing token cost/load.
3) KV-cache hardening: implement tenant-affinity buckets and short-lived TTL for low-frequency keys; introduce cache admission threshold to avoid storing single-use prefixes.
4) Admission & per-tenant budget: enforce soft per-tenant token budgets with probabilistic shedding once budget exhausted (graceful 429 with retry-after headers), plus burst credits for short spikes.
5) Autoscaler tuning & separate prewarm pool: split scaling into two signals - fast prewarm (short window, conservative capacity) and steady-state scale (existing smoothing). Add predictive priming based on trending slopes and tenant forecasts.
6) Telemetry & alerts: add a dedicated dashboard (latency by tenant, cache hit-rate by tenant, prewarm triggers) and an SLO alert when queued work grows > X tokens/minute for two consecutive sampling periods.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prewarm signal deploy reduces time-to-first-capacity by >= 70% for synthetic ramp tests.
- Soft-failure route is exercised in canary with 0.1% of traffic and returns schema-compatible responses; customers see reduced error rates during controlled capacity stress.
- KV-cache hit-rate improves by >=10% for workloads with noisy prefixes in replay tests.
- No regression to throughput or normal latencies in baseline workloads.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline & raw notes: https://confluence.redwoodinfra/internal/incidents/2026-03-06-gpu-capacity
- KV-cache proposal doc: https://confluence.redwoodinfra/internal/design/kv-cache-affinity
- Autoscaler design draft: https://drive.redwoodinfra/internal/autoscaler/prewarm-proposal-v1
- Canary plan & PRs: PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2401, https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-config/pull/189

Risks and trade-offs:
- Faster prewarm increases short-term cost (idle GPU minutes) if not tuned; we mitigate with conservative capacity and throttled prewarm.
- Soft-failure to a smaller model may change output quality for some customers; must be opt-out and only used when queue-based SLO is at risk.
- Tenant budgets introduce a complexity in billing/observability; need clear customer communication and dashboarding.

Next steps / Action items (owner, estimate):
- ENG-837203: Implement tenant-affinity buckets in KV cache (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 5)
- ENG-837204: Add fast prewarm signal and separate prewarm pool (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 8)
- ENG-837205: Implement per-tenant soft-budget admission and graded-degrade path (owner: Fahim Sattar, estimate: 8)
- Instrumentation & dashboards: (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3)
- Canary & runbook updates: (owner: Lin Chen, estimate: 3)

Status updates:
- 2026-03-10: Created ticket after incident retrospective. Initial design meeting scheduled.
- 2026-03-11: KV-cache affinity spike simulation completed; results show 12% hit-rate improvement in synthetic noisy-prefix workload. (artifact: https://artifacts.redwoodinfra/kv-sims/2026-03-11)
- 2026-03-12: Prototype prewarm signal implemented in branch runtime/prewarm-proto; initial canary plan drafted. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2401.
- 2026-03-13: Decided to make soft-failure opt-out for enterprise tenants and expose bumpable burst credits in dashboard. Follow-up: legal/comms review for customer-facing behavior.

Open questions:
- Threshold tuning: what is the right token-queue threshold for triggering soft-failure vs prewarm? (action: run 5x synthetic replay scenarios and propose default).
- Billing clarity: how do burst credits interact with reserved capacity customers? (action: PM review, assigned to Sofia Kaplan).
